_about: Data the phone/desktop app and the Roku app both use. Edit it here, run `python shared/generate.py`, and commit the result: that writes lib/src/generated/app_data.dart and roku/app/source/generated/app_data.brs (and the Roku's icon images come from `icon` via roku/tools/make_assets.py). CI fails if the generated files are out of date. See DESIGN_NOTES.md, "Keeping the apps in sync".

sports._about: By the API's sport id. `name` overrides the API's name (we say Soccer and Football); `icon` is a Material icon name (Flutter's Icons.<name>).

backends._about: The site the apps list and play from (see DESIGN_NOTES, Backends): `backend` picks one, and each has its own adapter in both apps. Per backend: api, its address; sportIds, its category names to our sport ids (sports above, for names and icons; unknown categories show under their own name with the default icon); logoCrops, where a site without team badges puts each team's logo on its game posters, for the title's first and second team, as fractions of the poster (left, top, width, height), cut out as the badges (optional); sources, stream sources best first (streams are grouped by source in this order, unknown ones last in the order the site gives them), with a description where the site gives one.

player._about: Player numbers both apps follow. rowThisGame / rowRecent: how many cards each side of the streams row shows. recentsKept: how many recent games are remembered (finished ones are dropped when the row is shown). stuckDownloadMs: a segment download still running this long (and, on phone/desktop, receiving nothing) gets a second copy. overlayPercent: how opaque the black behind the player's overlays is (title bar, streams pill and row, fallback note), the same for all of them. Phone and desktop only, switching between a source's separate quality feeds (the TV has the bandwidth and stays on the best): downPercent, down when segments download in under this much of their length's time (110: barely keeping up); never back up by itself (since 1.0.118: each switch is a gap, and it flapped on a swinging connection): instead, once segments have come in this much faster than the better feed needs (upPercent) for upHoldMs straight (doubled after an up that didn't hold), a button offers it for as long as that holds, with the title bar, and the first time for a stream by itself for upOfferMs. A stream with no lower feed of its own steps down to the game's SD stream instead (ppv's 540p copy), loaded afresh like a fallback, and the HD one is offered back the same way. weakStalls / weakStallWindowMs: this many freezes for want of video within the window, however short each, count as a weak connection (a step down, or the note): 2 s in every 5 never made one 3 s freeze (2026-11-01, in the car). slowStartMs: how long a stream may take to start before the spinner says why. failedForMinutes: how long a stream that failed (never started, or reconnecting gave up) says so where its quality goes, through restarts, unless it plays again; meanwhile it sorts after the working ones in the streams row and falling back tries it last. TV only, tvDryPauseAt: with fewer seconds than this in hand past the picture and nothing new coming, the TV pauses itself, a spinner over the dimmed picture, instead of running dry (the Roku blanks the picture and replays when it does); on again with tvCushionSecs in hand. tvStartFillSecs: before a start (new stream, reconnect or restart) first plays, it fills to this much, what the player holds plus segments downloaded for it it hasn't taken (its own buffer fills by size, ~13 s at 12.8 Mbps), or on with tvCushionSecs once nothing more comes for 6 s; the user would rather a long first spinner than any once live (22: the holes in ppv's feed that froze it once refilled were 12-18 s, 2026-11-01; one past 20 s restarts at live and throws the cushion away anyway, so more would only spin for nothing) (or this plus the next hold's step, if more), the cushion that rides out the source's own stalls (ppv's dipped up to 9 s and caught up again, 2026-11-01; refilled to 6-8 s, the next dip froze it again); or with at least this plus the step once nothing more has come for 5 s while downloaded segments wait untaken (the player's buffer full, as on a higher-bitrate stream; with none waiting it's the source that stalled, and it keeps waiting). tvRoamTroubles / tvRoamWindowMs / tvRoamEveryMs (TV only for now): this many signs of a struggling source server (a playlist slow enough that the player is served the last one, or the picture's clock skipping ahead) within tvRoamWindowMs find a new link in the background, used only if it's on a different server and not one that struggled within tvRoamAvoidMs; at most every tvRoamEveryMs (sooner after a link it turned down). tvBackCheckMs / tvBackChecks (TV only): fallen back from the stream picked, it's looked for this often in a background browser session, and offered once it has worked this many times in a row; phone and desktop have no stream server to look with. tvQuietRestartMs (TV only): spinning mid-game with the player asking for nothing at all this long, or 2 segment lengths if longer (no request, and none still being answered), it starts again at live on the same link instead of waiting out the 20 s stall and a full reconnect (2026-11-01 16:21, after ppv's clock went back: silent 19 s, 54 s off the picture); a healthy player's requests came up to 6.3 s apart on NFL Network's ~4.8 s segments, 2026-11-04. viewersRefreshMs: while playing, the title bar's viewer count (where the backend counts) is asked for afresh this often, and when the game opens.

updates._about: How often the apps look for a newer release while running: the Roku on a timer, the desktop app on Home only (when its window gets focus, and on coming back to Home). Android updates through Obtainium.

layout._about: Screen spacing, in pixels of a 1920-wide screen: the Roku draws at exactly that, and the desktop app (which scales its 1360-wide layout to the window) takes the same share of the width. margin: either side of the TV's screen, wide to stay clear of a TV's cropped edges. desktopMargin: the desktop's, smaller (a monitor shows its edges), both beside and above the screen's title, as the TV's title sits about as far from the top as from the side. gap: between cards side by side. sectionGap: above each section's heading.

playerIcons._about: The player's icons, the same on every app (Material icon names, as for sports). streamsPill: a row of cards, what the pill opens, rather than an arrow for which way (a press on the Roku, a tap elsewhere). switched: the note after falling back. weakConnection: the note when the connection can't keep up and there's no lower quality (phone and desktop). qualityUp: the button offering a source's better feed (phone and desktop).

playerText._about: The player's wording, the same on every app. {stream} is a stream's name and HD/SD, e.g. "Delta 1 (HD)"; {quality} a feed's resolution, e.g. "540p"; {n} a number. failed*: a stream that recently failed, where its quality would go (see player.failedForMinutes). switching*, upAvailable, weakConnection, slow* and retry are phone and desktop only (see player); siteUnreachable: the lists couldn't be loaded (the site's API answered with an error), on Home and the game and stream lists. streamBack: the stream picked works again after a fallback (TV only for now, see player.tvBackCheckMs). tv* the Roku's (tvFillPercent: inside the spinner while a start fills to player.tvStartFillSecs).
playerText.slowConnection: Still loading · your connection is slow
playerText.slowSource: Still loading · the stream is slow to respond
playerText.tvRetryKeys: Press OK to try again, or Back to pick another stream.

palette._about: Colours both apps draw with. `dark` is the dark theme (the Roku's only one); `light`, where given, is the phone/desktop light theme's version of the same colour.
